<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/understanding-preloaded-enrollment-ca-certificates","lastmod":"2026-06-01T12:43Z","nid":"1483701"} -->
## Understanding Preloaded Enrollment (CA) Certificates

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-preloaded-enrollment-ca-certificates
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Certificate Management > Enrollment Certificates > Understanding Preloaded Enrollment (CA) Certificates
- Last modified: 2026-06-01T12:43Z
- Summary: Information on the preloaded Zscaler-issued signing certificates within the Zscaler Admin Console that can be used for App Connector and Zscaler Client Connector enrollment.

[Watch a video about Enrollment Certificates](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/iframe/gstgspmdcw) (shows legacy UI).

The following Zscaler-issued signing certificates can be used to enroll Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors:

- Root: The root (i.e., parent) certificate for the Client and Connector signing certificates.
- Client: A Private Access signing certificate that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connector. The certificate's trust is established by the Zscaler public key infrastructure (PKI). Its parent certificate is the Zscaler Root certificate. Private Access (ZPA) automatically uses this to sign certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connector, unless you configure another Zscaler-issued certificate.
- Connector: A signing certificate for Private Access that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connectors. The certificate's trust is also established by the Zscaler PKI.

[Image: Enrollment Certificates page with preloaded Zscaler-issued CA certificates displayed]

These signing certificates are 2048-bit key RSA certificates, which support TLS 1.2 connections (with cipher suite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256).

The certificate used to enroll a Private Service Edge must have the same root certificate used by the enrollment certificate for enrolling App Connectors and Zscaler Client Connector. To learn more, see [About Enrollment (CA) Certificates](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-EnrollmentCertificates), [Configuring Private Service Edges](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-service-edges), and [Generating Zscaler-Issued Enrollment (CA) Certificates](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-generateEnrollmentCertificate).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/understanding-private-access-architecture","lastmod":"2026-06-01T09:15Z","nid":"1484551"} -->
## Understanding the Private Access Architecture

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-private-access-architecture
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Understanding the Private Access Architecture
- Last modified: 2026-06-01T09:15Z
- Summary: Information on the Private Access service and key components.

Private Access (ZPA) was built from the ground up to provide secure remote access. To learn more about the Zscaler security platform and Internet & SaaS (ZIA) architecture, see [Understanding the Zscaler Cloud Architecture for Internet & SaaS](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-cloud-architecture).

Private Access runs on a unique multi-tenant infrastructure, separate from that of Internet & SaaS, to make the service highly available. This separation ensures that when the same organization is using both services, public and internal traffic never mix on the same device. Additional measures are used to ensure security and privacy between organizations using the Private Access service, and in many cases, traversing the same equipment. Finally, all communication is encrypted end to end.

The Private Access service includes the following key components and subsystems:

- Private Access Central Authority
- Public Service Edges and Private Service Edges
- App Connectors
- Traffic Forwarding
- Logging Streaming Service

## Understanding Communication Between Components and Subsystems

All communication between Private Access components travel within a mutually pinned, client and server certificate-verified TLS connection. Within this TLS-encrypted Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel), a microtunneling protocol exists. Select components of Private Access run through this encrypted Microtunnel end to end.

Because client and server use pinned certificates, it is cryptographically impossible for Private Access to experience a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack. The client certificates are verified against an organization's Certificate Authority (CA) and the server certificates are verified against Zscaler's CA, which cannot be spoofed by any third-party compromised CA.

All Zscaler certificates are signed through an offline-only, air-gapped, signing ceremony. Private Access only accepts connections from Zscaler Client Connector and the App Connector instances that present a client certificate signed by a CA associated with each tenant. Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector will only connect to Private Access service components that present a certificate signed by the Private Access infrastructure PKI.

All certificates used within the Private Access infrastructure, including all organization-operated systems, have private keys that never leave the physical device in which they were generated. The private keys for each organization's Central Authority (CA) are stored in encrypted format (i.e., AES256-GCM). Proper best practices for public key lifecycles are always maintained.

### Zscaler Tunnel

A Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) is a TLS-encrypted, mutually authenticated point-to-point connection between Zscaler Client Connector and a Public Service Edge managed by Zscaler, or it's between an App Connector and a Private Service Edge managed by an organization. A Z-Tunnel does not contain any direct IP data. An additional Z-Tunnel is created between Zscaler Client Connector and a Public Service Edge, or between an App Connector and a Private Service Edge, to support [multi-tenancy in Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-client-connector-support-multiple-tenants). This allows Zscaler Client Connector to establish a Z-Tunnel with the tenant and establish a separate Z-Tunnel with the partner tenant. The second Z-Tunnel works without any additional setup or configuration. Also, the Z-Tunnel can carry within it multiple communication channels called Microtunnels.

Z-Tunnels are authenticated using public key cryptography. Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors are authenticated with the organization's public key infrastructure (PKI). Public Service Edges and Private Service Edges are authenticated with Zscaler's PKI. In addition to the certificate-based authentication already applied, the Z-Tunnel is further authenticated using SAML 2.0.

### Microtunnel

A Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) is an end-to-end communication channel created between Zscaler Client Connector and an internal application via a Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge and an App Connector upon demand.

An M-Tunnel originates in Zscaler Client Connector when traffic from a client application (i.e., a web browser or SSH client) attempts to connect to an application server, which is associated with a synthetic IP address. The M-Tunnel extends to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge using a tag created by Zscaler Client Connector. The M-Tunnel then extends to the appropriate App Connector using a different tag chosen by that connector. Finally, the App Connector connects the M-Tunnel to the actual application server providing the service originally requested by the client application.

At no point in the communication is actual IP identification data passed. Instead, the combination of tags created by Zscaler Client Connector and the App Connector function similarly to the label stack in a Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) network. Just as in an MPLS network, where the label-switched path (LSP) uniquely identifies a connection, Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector tags identify a unique connection for each application request.

The Private Access Central Authority (CA) is the brain and nervous system of the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE). It is a geographically distributed system of in-sync nodes that all actively service requests. To learn more, see [Public Service Edges and the Central Authority](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-service-edges#ServiceEdgeCentralAuthority).

The Private Access CA monitors the ZTE and provides a central location for software and database updates, as well as policy and configuration settings. Each component of the system is aware of the health of the entire ZTE, and policy is distributed across all components of the CA. It includes user interfaces connected via APIs to configuration components, as well as distributed dispatchers that track real-time application states.

Public Service Edges and Private Service Edges enforce user policies and provide secure transport to App Connectors. Maintained by Zscaler and deployed globally, Public Service Edges are the cloud-based portion of the Private Access data forwarding path, responsible for giving Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors the ability to provide secure, authenticated, policy-based access to internal applications. Private Service Edges act in the same capacity, but they are managed by an organization. Public Service Edges and Private Service Edges are responsible for a variety of functions, including:

- Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector configuration and authentication, using public key cryptography.

Public Service Edges and Private Service Edges use only public keys for authenticating all remote systems and clients connecting with it. No private keys are stored or used, with the exception of the Public Service Edge's or Private Service Edge's identity.

- Creating and managing Microtunnels (M-Tunnels), including authentication, policy, setup, teardown, and data forwarding. M-Tunnels​​​​​ are end-to-end encrypted connections designed to ensure that all traffic stays separate. To learn more, see Understanding Communication Between Components and Subsystems below.

To learn more, see [Understanding Service Edges](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-service-edges).

App Connectors provide the authenticated secure interface between an organization's application servers and the ZTE. App Connectors can be distributed using lightweight virtual machines (VM) to run in legacy enterprise data centers and public cloud environments, or as a package that can be installed under supported operating systems.

App Connectors are deployed in locations where internal applications reside, or they can be deployed in any location that has connectivity to those applications. Private Access selects the closest App Connector given the location of the user and the App Connector-to-application latency. It is best to install them in redundant (N+1) configurations, where (N) is the number of App Connectors required to support the applications, because they are always active. App Connectors never communicate with each other and do not accept inbound connections. They only require an outbound connection to the internet to reach Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges, so they can provide users access to internal applications in your organization.

Using a key pair (i.e., a provisioning key and a corresponding TLS client certificate), the App Connector and the ZTE verify each other as part of enrollment. After an App Connector is enrolled, the TLS client certificate allows it to maintain its authentication with the nearest Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge, which provides the App Connector with its configuration and allows it to begin its operational tasks. These tasks include:

- Find applications as requested by users.
- Act on behalf of the application to send traffic back to users.
- Complete DNS requests on demand, based on established policies.
- Monitor applications for their reachability.

To learn more, see [About App Connectors](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-connectors).

There are two ways to manage traffic forwarding:

- Zscaler Client Connector
- Browser Access

Zscaler Client Connector is a client or app that is installed on a user's device (or endpoint), which authenticates the endpoint with the ZTE and enables access to internal applications on behalf of that endpoint. Zscaler Client Connector verifies the integrity of both the Private Access infrastructure and the peers it communicates with using public key cryptography.

Beyond the full authentication, as handled as part of the standard SAML 2.0 workflow, Zscaler Client Connector creates a unique fingerprint of the user's device. This means if someone copies Zscaler Client Connector from one device to another, the fingerprint generated by Zscaler Client Connector will prevent successful enrollment from the new device.

Zscaler Client Connector recognizes the internal applications that are available via Private Access. Access to these applications is defined in Private Access based on policies. Using information received from the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge, it intercepts the user requests for those applications, and then forwards those requests to the ZTE. No network information is required to access available applications, and an organization can specify if resources must go through Private Access at all times, when on an untrusted network only, or never.

To facilitate secure private connections that are abstracted from the physical network, Zscaler Client Connector associates permitted internal applications with a set of synthetic IP addresses. When a client application (i.e., a web browser or SSH client) sends out a DNS request, Zscaler Client Connector recognizes the domain as an internal application being protected by Private Access. Zscaler Client Connector then intercepts the DNS request and delivers a DNS response to the client application that uses the synthetic IP address associated with the internal application.

Organizations can also use Zscaler Client Connector to direct user traffic to Internet & SaaS. Zscaler Client Connector identifies internal applications to forward traffic to Private Access, and other traffic goes to Internet & SaaS. If an organization is using Internet & SaaS and Private Access, Zscaler Client Connector inherits some functionality from Internet & SaaS, including enrollment, user profiles, traffic management, etc. However, organizations do not need access to Internet & SaaS to use Private Access. To learn more, see [What Is Zscaler Client Connector?](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/what-is-zscaler-client-connector)

Browser Access allows you to leverage a web browser for user authentication and application access over Private Access. This allows access to applications over Private Access for users who cannot install Zscaler Client Connector on their devices.

The application must be available via HTTP/HTTPS in a web browser that supports TLS 1.2. When a user tries to access an internal web application, they can open any web browser on their device and enter the application's URL. Private Access directs this traffic to the organization's identity provider (IdP), where the IdP authenticates the user and grants a SAML certificate before forwarding the traffic to a Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. Browser Access is session based, so the user must authenticate via the IdP every time they try to access the web application.

The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge accepts the SAML certificate and applies all policies, making only permissioned internal web applications accessible to the user. If the policy allows the user access, Private Access identifies the best-path App Connector for the internal web application and connects them to it. When the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge sends out a request to all App Connectors sitting at the application level, the App Connector sitting closest to the internal web application responds by connecting to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge.

The connections from user to Public Service Edge (or Private Service Edge) and App Connector to Public Service Edge (or Private Service Edge) are then stitched together forming a TLS-encrypted tunnel, creating a secure channel between the authorized user and the internal web application without granting network access.

To learn more, see [About Browser Access](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-browser-access).

The Log Streaming Service (LSS) provides real-time and historical visibility into the operation of Private Access by analyzing events reported, primarily by the Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges. In addition to real-time analytics and status, the LSS provides short- and long-term storage.

Information sent to the LSS includes user activity and status, App Connector status, and HTTP information related to Browser Access. The default fields in log templates created by Private Access include personally identifiable information (PII), however, your organization can create a custom log template that only captures specific fields.

The LSS has two components: a log receiver and an App Connector. It can stream logs from your Private Access tenant to a SIEM or log receiver you manage. You must specify the logs required for streaming in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Because Private Access was purpose built to ensure secure, private access to internal applications, the service does not store any information on any type of persistent media (i.e., disk) unless it is configured to do so by your organization. The information can also be obfuscated based on your organization's preferences.

To learn more, see [About Log Streaming Service](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-log-streaming-service).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Understanding Private Access Session Status Codes

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-private-access-session-status-codes
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Dashboard & Diagnostics > Applications & Users Monitoring > Understanding Private Access Session Status Codes
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T11:11Z
- Summary: Information on session status codes that appear in the Diagnostics pages of the Zscaler Admin Console.

Private Access (ZPA) session status codes appear on the [User Activity Diagnostics](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-user-activity-diagnostics) page. Each table has its own search field and can be sorted by column.

Status codes are prefixed by the related Private Access component:

- AC: The App Connector component.
- CA: The Central Authority component.
- CLT: The Zscaler Client Connector component.
- SE: The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access component.
- ZPA BA: The Browser Access service.

The types of session status codes available are:

- Error Codes
- Info Codes
- Policy Block Codes

The following is a list of Error status codes:

| Session Status | Internal Reason | Description | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC: App Connector in paused state for upgrade | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_AST_IN_PAUSE_STATE_FOR_UPGRADE | The App Connector is in a paused state for upgrade. The App Connector returns to a normal state after the upgrade completes. | No action required. |
| AC: Application Segment not configured | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_APP_NOT_FOUND | The App Connector cannot set up a connection to the server because it cannot find the application in the configuration database. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Application’s Microtunnel request failed due to exceeding the rate limit. | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_RATE_LIMIT_REACHED | The App Connector rejected the application’s Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) request because the rate limit threshold for the specific domain was exceeded. To learn more, see [Ranges & Limitations](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/ranges-limitations#private-applications). | Try again later. If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Cannot open connection to server | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_OPEN_SERVER_CONN | The App Connector encountered an error when setting up a data connection to the server. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the application. |
| AC: Cannot open connection to Service Edge | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_OPEN_BROKER_CONN | The App Connector encountered an error when opening a connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. |
| AC: Cannot setup connection to Service Edge | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_INIT_FOHH_MCONN | The App Connector encountered an error when setting up a connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge, and then ask the user to request the application. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Connection between server and App Connector was closed | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_OPEN_SERVER_CLOSE | During data connection setup, the connection from the server to the App Connector was closed. | Verify if the application is reachable from the App Connector, and check the available server capacity |
| AC: Connection database is full | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_HASH_TBL_FULL | The App Connector cannot set up a connection to the server because the connection database is full. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Connection request timed out | AST_MT_SETUP_TIMEOUT | The App Connector timed out while setting up a connection. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the application. |
| AC: Connection request to server timed out | AST_MT_SETUP_TIMEOUT_CANNOT_CONN_TO_SERVER | The App Connector timed out while waiting for a connection response from the server. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the application. |
| AC: Connection request to Service Edge timed out | AST_MT_SETUP_TIMEOUT_CANNOT_CONN_TO_BROKER | The App Connector cannot set up a data connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ensure that the App Connector is able to reach the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. |
| AC: CPU Limit Exceeded for PRA Connection | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_CPU_LIMIT_REACHED | The App Connector CPU limit is exceeded for a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) connection. No more PRA connections are allowed. | Add cores to the App Connector or add additional App Connectors. Contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| AC: Disabled in Admin Portal | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_AST_CFG_DISABLE | The Microtunnel setup has failed because the App Connector has been disabled in the Zscaler Admin Console. | No action required. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Maximum PRA Session Limit Reached | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_MAX_SESSIONS_REACHED | The maximum session limit is reached for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) connections on the App Connector. | Add cores and memory to the App Connector or add additional App Connectors. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Memory Limit Exceeded for PRA Connection | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_MEM_LIMIT_REACHED | The App Connector memory limit is exceeded for a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) connection. No more PRA connections are allowed. | Add memory to the App Connector or add additional App Connectors. Contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| AC: Service Edge not responding to connection request from App Connector | AST_MT_SETUP_TIMEOUT_NO_ACK_TO_BIND | App Connector is unable to setup a data connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. The App Connector timed out while waiting for a connection response from the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: DNS resolution failed | INVALID_DOMAIN | None of the App Connectors configured for the application could successfully resolve the hostname within three seconds of sending a DNS request. This might be because of a DNS resolution failure on the App Connector or a misconfigured DNS in the DC environment.; The App Connector resolves DNS successfully, but the health check fails. This might happen because the App Connector cannot reach the application server over the network or the App Connector can reach the application server, but the server is rejecting the health check. | Ensure that the hostname is correctly configured.; Verify the App Connector can consistently resolve DNS for the hostname.; Check that the App Connector can reach the application server and the server accepts requests on the expected ports.; Ensure that services between the App Connector and the application server (e.g., access control lists, host-based firewalls, etc.) allow them to communicate on the expected ports and protocols. |
| AC: DNS resolution failed for unmonitored app | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_NO_DNS_TO_SERVER | The end host (not a proxy or a configured server group) is not resolvable. The code only comes up in a specific use case when there is all of the following: No-health application; Dynamic server discovery is enabled (i.e., no server group configured); The target application has failed to resolve | Execute the Linux Shell Command with the URL that failed in the transaction to understand why the DNS resolution is failing, and why the App Connector is failing the DNS. |
| AC: Duplicate connection tag ID | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_DUP_MT_ID | The App Connector cannot set up a data connection because another data connection with the same tag ID already exists. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error connecting to server | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_OPEN_SERVER_ERROR | The App Connector experienced an error while setting up a data connection to a specific server. This was because the application server closed the connection with TCP Reset (RST), the server was not listening on the port, or the App Connector did not support PRA. | Verify if the application is reachable from the App Connector, check the available server capacity, or contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| AC: Error connecting to server due to missing PRA support on App Connector | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_PRA_UNAVAILABLE | The App Connector experienced an error while setting up a PRA connection. This was because the App Connector did not support PRA. | Enable the necessary subcomponent for PRA on your App Connector group. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error in creating Service Edge-server connection | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_CONN_PEER | The App Connector encountered an error when connecting the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge and server connections. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error in data connection to Service Edge | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BROKER_BIND_FAIL | The App Connector encountered an error when setting up a data connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error in local connection | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BIND_TO_AST_LOCAL_OWNER | The App Connector processing the data connection request has encountered an error. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error in non local connection | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BIND_GLOBAL_OWNER | The App Connector processing the data connection request encountered an error. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Error processing response from Service Edge | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BIND_ACK | The connection confirmation from the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge has an error. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: File descriptors are exhausted | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_NO_SYSTEM_FD | The transaction failed as the operating system has run out of file descriptors. | Increase the number of file descriptors that are available on the host. To learn more, see [Monitoring App Connector Performance](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/monitoring-connector-performance). |
| AC: File descriptors are exhausted for App Connector process | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_NO_PROCESS_FD | The transaction failed as the App Connector processing could not secure additional file descriptors from the operating system. | Increase the number of App Connectors in the App Connector group.To learn more, see [Adding App Connectors to an Existing App Connector Group](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/adding-connectors-existing-connector-group).  If the App Connector group is set up for a wildcard application, try [creating more application segments](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-defined-application-segments) along with App Connector groups in order to have greater load distribution across the App Connector groups. |
| AC: Service Edge database is full | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL | The App Connector cannot set up a connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge because the connection database is full. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| AC: Source ports are exhausted | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_NO_EPHEMERAL_PORT | The transaction failed as the operating system has run out of source ports. | Increase the number of ports. To learn more, see [Monitoring App Connector Performance](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/monitoring-connector-performance). |
| AC: Timeout connecting to server | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_OPEN_SERVER_TIMEOUT | App Connector timed out while setting up a data connection to a specific server. | Verify if the application is reachable from the App Connector, and check the application latency. |
| AC: Disabled Web probe | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_WEBPROBE_HTTPS_DISABLED | The Web probe request cannot be sent to the App Connector because the Web probe is disabled. | Enable the Web probe. |
| CA: App Connector health information request timed out | DSP_MT_SETUP_FAIL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT | The health information request timed out when attempting to reach the App Connector. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. |
| CA: App Connector is not available | NO_CONNECTOR_AVAILABLE | None of the App Connectors are configured to reach this application.; None of the App Connectors have learned the configuration for this application even though the application is associated with App Connectors through configuration.; The application was just configured or the App Connector has just restarted and is still learning its configuration.; The App Connector is unable to learn its configuration from the Private Access certificate authority (CA). | Ensure that at least one App Connector group is configured to reach this application.; Ask the user to access the application again. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CA: Application is not available | APP_NOT_AVAILABLE | The application segment is not configured for access. | Ensure that the application segment is configured in the Zscaler Admin Console.; Ask the user to access the application again. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CA: Application is not reachable | APP_NOT_REACHABLE | None of the App Connectors configured for the application can reach the server. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the server. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CA: Cannot find tunnels for ZPA Public Service Edge | ZPN_ERR_EXTRANET_NO_TUNNEL_AVAILABLE | No eligible tunnels were found to send user information to. | Verify and validate tunnel information. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CA: Error communicating with Service Edge | DSP_MT_SETUP_FAIL_CANNOT_SEND_TO_BROKER | The path selection service is unable to communicate with the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | Ask the user to access the application again. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CA: Missing information for continuous health reporting | DSP_MT_SETUP_FAIL_MISSING_HEALTH | The App Connector was unable to process the continuous health report due to missing health information. | Ensure that the App Connector can reach the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. |
| CA: Missing locations | ZPN_ERR_EXTRANET_NO_LOCATIONS_ASSOCIATED | No locations were found for the associated application. | Select a valid location for the associated application. |
| CLT: Connection failed | CLT_CONN_FAILED | The incoming TCP connection failed. | Verify that the application is listening on the port. |
| CLT: DoubleEncrypt not supported | CLT_DOUBLEENCRYPT_NOT_SUPPORTED | The double encryption of the incoming Microtunnel request is not supported by the Zscaler Client Connector. | Do not configure the application segment applying remote assistance to use double encryption. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Duplicate tag | CLT_DUPLICATE_TAG | The tag ID is used in the Zscaler Client Connector. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Invalid client | CLT_INVALID_CLIENT | The receiving Zscaler Client Connector device doesn't match with the request. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Invalid domain | CLT_INVALID_DOMAIN | The FQDN destination host doesn't match the receiving Zscaler Client Connector detected. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Invalid tag | CLT_INVALID_TAG | The tag ID is not designed for the incoming Microtunnel flow. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Multiple clients registered with the same domain | MULTIPLE_CLIENT_REGISTRATIONS_FOR_DOMAIN | Zscaler Client Connector rejected the connection request due to multiple clients registered with the same domain. | Try again later. Ensure that no two clients are registered with the same domain. If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Port unreachable | CLT_PORT_UNREACHABLE | The port is not listening. | Verify that the application is running on the port or remove the port in the application configuration. |
| CLT: Probe failed | CLT_PROBE_FAILED | The port probe failed. | Verify that the application is running on the port or remove the port in the application configuration. |
| CLT: Protocol not supported | CLT_PROTOCOL_NOT_SUPPORTED | The IP protocol of the incoming Microtunnel request is not supported by the Zscaler Client Connector. | Verify that the initiating client machine does connect to the receiving Zscaler Client Connector with a protocol other than TCP, UDP, or ICMP. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Read failed | CLT_READ_FAILED | The Zscaler Client Connector local socket read failed. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| CLT: Wrong port | CLT_WRONG_PORT | The incoming Microtunnel request asks for the listening ports of the Zscaler Client Connector itself. | Verify that the initiating client machine does not connect to the receiving Zscaler Client Connector listening ports. |
| SE: App Connector disabled via Private Service Edge | ZPN_ERR_AUTH_SERVICE_DISABLED | The Private Service Edge disabled the App Connector. | Ensure that the App Connector is able to reach the Private Service Edge. |
| SE: App Connector group not configured | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_CONNECTOR_GROUPS_MISSING | The Public Service Edge was unable to process the application request since an App Connector group was not specified in the Server group configuration. | Edit the server group to add the App Connector groups. To learn more, see [Editing Server Groups](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-server-groups). |
| SE: Application access blocked because user was not active with SCIM | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_SCIM_INACTIVE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge has failed to set up the data connection due to the user being deactivated or not synced in SCIM. | Ask an admin to sync user accounts via SCIM to activate users. To learn more, see [About SCIM](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-scim). If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Application approval policy blocked access | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REJECTED_BY_POLICY_APPROVAL | The Private Access service blocked the application request because the user isn't allowed to access the application at this time. | Update the approval policy to allow the user access in the time window. |
| SE: Application not configured | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_APP_NOT_FOUND | The Public Service Edge or the Private Service Edge cannot set up a connection since the application is not configured. | Ensure that the application and application segment is configured in the Zscaler Admin Console.; Ask the user to access the application again. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Authentication failed due to insufficient memory | BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_CANNOT_ADD_ATTR_TO_HEAP | Authentication failed because of insufficient memory to process the SAML response. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Authentication failed due to insufficient resources | BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_CANNOT_ADD_ATTR_TO_HASH | Authentication failed because of insufficient resources to process the SAML response. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Authentication level expired | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REAUTH_EXPIRED_WITH_AL | The Public Service Edge was unable to process the application request since the Authentication Level (for Step-Up Authentication) expired. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Authentication Level required | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REAUTH_WITH_AL | The Public Service Edge was unable to process the application request since the user does not have the required Authentication Level. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Authentication unsuccessful | BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_FAILURE | The user's authentication to Private Access was unsuccessful. | The user must authenticate with valid credentials. |
| SE: B2B Federated application access failed | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_B2B_ACCESS_DENIED | Application access for the Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation was denied. | No action required. Contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| SE: B2B Federated application access is terminated due to connectivity issues | BRK_MT_TERMINATED_B2B_BROKER_CHANGED | The active connection for B2B Federation was terminated due to network connectivity issues, or the B2B Federation status was changed. | No action required. Contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| SE: Cannot complete data connection setup | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_CANNOT_SEND_MT_COMPLETE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge encountered an error when processing the data connection request from Zscaler Client Connector or the App Connector. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Cannot find ZIA Public Service Edge to service the request | BRK_MT_BROKER_REQUEST_ZVPN_NOT_FOUND | Cannot find the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS to service the request. | No action required. If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| SE: Cannot send Microtunnel request | BRK_MT_ZVPN_ERROR | The Public Service Edge for Private Access cannot process the Microtunnel request. | No action required. If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support to learn more. |
| SE: Cannot send Microtunnel request as Extranet client is disabled for tenant | BRK_MT_REJECT_EXTRANET_CLIENT_NOT_ENABLED | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge rejected the Microtunnel request because Extranet is disabled for your tenant. | Contact Zscaler Support to enable Extranet for your tenant. |
| SE: Cannot send Microtunnel request for Extranet application as Extranet is disabled | BRK_MT_REJECT_EXTRANET_NOT_ENABLED | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge rejected the Microtunnel request because Extranet is disabled. | Contact Zscaler Support to enable Extranet feature for the customer to continue sending Microtunnel requests. |
| SE: Cannot send Microtunnel request to Extranet application as Extranet is hard disabled. | BRK_MT_REJECT_HARD_DISABLED_EXTRANET | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge rejected the Microtunnel request because Extranet is hard disabled. | Contact Zscaler Support to remove the hard disable feature flag for Extranet to continue sending Microtunnel requests. |
| SE: Error in promoting connection to Public Service Edge | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_CANNOT_PROMOTE | The Private Service Edge cannot promote the application tunnel to the Public Service Edge. The Public Service Edge might be unreachable, or the Private Service Edge is setting up a data connection with the Public Service Edge. | No action required. If the problem persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Exceeded limit or connection request attempts | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REPEATED_DISPATCH | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was unable to establish a data connection within the limit of the connection request attempts. | If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Just-in-Time Approval timed out | BRK_MT_TERMINATED_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge terminated the session and caused a timeout due to approval time window expiration. | Ask the user to access the application in the approved time window. Update the approvals for the user. |
| SE: Maximum workload groups exceeded | BRK_MT_REJECT_MAX_WTAG_EXCEEDED | The workload groups have exceeded the maximum limit. To learn more, see [Ranges & Limitations](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/ranges-limitations#private-applications). | Reduce the number of workload groups. |
| SE: Remote assistance connection expired | C2C_CLIENT_CONN_EXPIRED | The client connection expired during the initiation of a remote assistance session. | To learn more, contact Zscaler Support. |

This was not a security problem. | ZIA_MT_BLOCKED_BY_SYSTEM_ERROR | Internet & SaaS inspection was performed, but there was an internal system problem. | ZPA BA: Cert Chaining Issue | EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_CERT_CHAIN_ISSUE | Private Access is not able to validate the chain of trust for the server certificate configured for this application. | Upload the web server certificate including the entire chain of trust for the certificate. |

| ZPA BA: TLS setup failed with peer | EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_PEER | The Browser Access service cannot set up a HTTPS connection towards the web server due to an issue occurring during TLS setup. | The issue is most likely due to an invalid web server certificate being used. | ZPA BA: TLS Wrong Version Number | EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_VERSION_MISMATCH | A TLS version mismatch between Private Access and the Browser Access-enabled application occurred. This happens when the web server is running TLS 1.0/1.1 or earlier versions. | Enable TLS 1.2 on the web server. |

The following is a list of Info status codes:

| Session Status | Internal Reason | Description | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC: Connection closed successfully | AST_MT_TERMINATED | The connection to the App Connector was terminated without issue. | No action required. |
| SE: App Connector disconnected to ZPA Private Service Edge | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_AST_PBRK_DATA_DOWN | The Private Service Edge connection to the App Connector was disconnected. | Ensure that the App Connector is able to reach the Private Service Edge. |
| SE: Connection closed by App Connector | BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_ASSISTANT | The App Connector closed the application Microtunnel (M-Tunnel) as a result of the application server terminating the TCP session with a TCP FIN. | No action required. |
| SE: Callback for Server Name Indication maxed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_SNI_SLOW | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection closed because the maximum number of Server Name Indication (SNI) callbacks was reached. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection closed by server | BRK_MT_RESET_FROM_SERVER | The application server terminated the connection with TCP RST. | No action required. |
| SE: Callback for Server Name Indication timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_SNI_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection is closed because the wait time for SNI callbacks has expired. | No action required. |
| SE: Client Connector TLS session not present | MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE_CLIENT_CLOSED | The connection from the Zscaler Client Connector to Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated, resulting in the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge terminating all application sessions for that Zscaler Client Connector. | No action required. |
| SE: App Connector TLS session not present | MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE_AST_CLOSED | The connection from the App Connector to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated, resulting in the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge terminating all application sessions for that App Connector. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection closed by Client Connector | BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_CLIENT | The connection from the App Connector to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated, resulting in the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge terminating all application sessions for that App Connector. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection closed by Service Edge | BRK_MT_TERMINATED | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge closed the application tunnel connection. This is part of the Service Edge’s regular process at the end of an application request. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection closed due to missing Server Name Indication | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_SNI_MISSING | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection is closed because the SNI is missing. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection closed successfully | MT_CLOSED_TERMINATED | The connection to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated without issue. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection failed because HTTP return code was not 200 | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_HTTP_RESPONSE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed because the returned code was not 200. The returned code 200 means that a connection is OK. If the code does not come back with 200, the connection is closed. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection redirected to another Service Edge | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_REDIRECT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was redirected to another Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection request timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_CONNECT_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge timed out while setting up a connection. This is not an error scenario, only a function of the service. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection request to server timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_RX_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection timed out while waiting for a connection response from the server. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge keeps the user's application session alive for the time interval specified by the Idle Connection Timeout prior to terminating the session. This is not an error scenario, only a function of the service. | No action required. |
| SE: Connection verification failed | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_CERT_VERIFY | The Public Service Edge or ZPA Private Service Edge connection was unable to verify the server certificate. | No action required. |
| SE: Data connection idle to App Connector | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_AST_DATA_CONN_FLOW_CONTROL | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge data connection was closed by App Connector because the connection was idle or blocked for more than 5 minutes. | No action required. |
| SE: Data connection idle to Service Edge | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_BRK_DATA_CONN_FLOW_CONTROL | The data connection was closed by the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge because the connection was idle or blocked for more than 5 minutes. | No action required. |
| SE: Deserialization error with callback | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_TLV_CALLBACK | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed due to a deserialization error. | If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Deserialization error with no callback | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_TLV_NO_CALLBACK | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed due to a deserialization error. | If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: End of file received, closing connection | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_SOCKET_CLOSE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed because the end of the file was received. This is not an error scenario, only a function of the service. | No action required. |
| SE: Flow control timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_DATA_CONN_FLOW_CONTROL | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed because flow control was blocked for more than 5 minutes. | No action required. |
| SE: Log channel reconnection timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_LOG_RECONN | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge reconnection to the log channels timed out because the reconnection timer expired. | No action required. |
| SE: Protocol data mismatched during parsing | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_TLV_LEN | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed during parsing due to a protocol data mismatch. | No action required. |
| SE: Proxy connection failed for HTTP response error 200 | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_PROXY_NOT_200 | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection through the proxy was closed because the returned code was not 200. The returned code 200 means that a connection is OK. If the code does not come back with 200, the connection is closed. | Check the proxy connection. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Proxy connection request timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_PROXY_TIMEOUT | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed because the connection through the proxy exceeded the proxy timeout value. | No action required. |
| SE: Proxy connection timed out | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_PROXY_IDLE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection closed because the connection through the proxy timed out. | No action required. |
| SE: Request was successful | OPEN_OR_ACTIVE_CONNECTION | The connection is active and working. | No action required. |
| SE: SSL context not found | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_SSL_CTX_NONE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection closed because it was unable to identify the SSL context. | No action required. |
| SE: Timeout policy closed idle connection | BRK_MT_TERMINATED_IDLE_TIMEOUT | If an idle timeout is configured, Private Access will keep the user's application session alive for the interval specified by the Idle Connection Timeout prior to terminating the session. This is not an error scenario, only a function of the service. | No action required. |
| SE: TLS session not present | MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge closed the application session because the parent TLS session to Zscaler Client Connector or the App Connector is no longer present. | Typically, application sessions are closed by the ZPA Public Service Edge or ZPA Private Service Edge when users disconnect from the service. Normally, no further action is required. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Unable to deserialize protocol data | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_TLV_DESERIALIZE | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed because the protocol data could not be deserialized. | If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| SE: Unexpected data connection to ZPA Private Service Edge | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_AST_PBRK_VERIFY_FAILED | The Private Service Edge connection was closed because the connection was made with a Private Service Edge different than the expected Private Service Edge. | No action required. |
| SE: User closed connection | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_OPS | The Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge connection was closed at the user’s request. | No action required. |
| SE: User disabled via SCIM | MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE_SCIM_USER_DISABLE | The Private Access service closed the connection due to the user being disabled via SCIM. | No action required. |
| SE: ZPA Private Service Edge configuration changed | FOHH_CLOSE_REASON_AST_PBRK_CTRL_CONN_CFG_CHG | The Private Service Edge connection was closed due to a change in the Private Service Edge configuration. | No action required. |

| Session Status | Internal Reason | Description | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SE: Application policy blocked access | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REJECTED_BY_POLICY | The Private Access service blocked the application request because the user isn't allowed to access the requested application. | Update the policy to allow the user. |
| SE: Application policy blocked access due to device failing a posture check | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_REJECTED_BY_POLICY_POSTURE_FAILED | The Private Access service blocked the application request because the device posture check failed. The device does not meet the required security posture criteria (e.g., missing security updates, disabled antivirus, etc.). | Confirm all security posture requirements are met for the device (e.g., update the operating system, enable antivirus software, etc.). |
| SE: Policy is not configured for access | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_NO_POLICY_FOUND | The Private Access service blocked the application request because a policy isn't configured for the requested application. The application request is also blocked when an application segment or a segment group is disabled. | Update the policy to allow the user. Enable the application segment and segment group. |
| SE: Timeout policy blocked access | BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_SAML_EXPIRED | The Private Access service blocked the application or Web Browser request because the timeout policy requires the user to authenticate. | The user must reauthenticate in Zscaler Client Connector. If needed, update the timeout policy to increase the interval before a timeout. To learn more, see [Configuring Timeout Policies](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-timeout-policies). |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/understanding-privileged-remote-access","lastmod":"2026-06-25T12:22Z","nid":"1485876"} -->
## Understanding Privileged Remote Access

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-privileged-remote-access
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Privileged Remote Access Management > Understanding Privileged Remote Access
- Last modified: 2026-06-25T12:22Z
- Summary: An overview of Privileged Remote Access (PRA) and its features within the Zscaler Admin Console.

Privileged Remote Access (PRA) is a clientless remote desktop gateway that enables end users to securely connect to servers, jump hosts and bastion hosts, or desktops using Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), Secure Shell (SSH), Virtual Network Computing (VNC), and RealVNC from the end user's modern browser without installing Zscaler Client Connector or any browser plugins. PRA allows you to provide third parties (vendors, contractors, suppliers), IT administrators, and remote employees controlled access to your privileged servers and applications.

Admins can set up specific end users for specific privileged consoles with policies for a specific time frame. You can also choose to provide configured credentials for short-term end users, or prompt end users to enter their credentials when using a privileged console. These PRA features provide secure, user-friendly access while also limiting the end user's access only to what is needed and when and for a duration of time.

To set up PRA, see [Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Privileged Remote Access](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/step-step-configuration-guide-privileged-remote-access).

## Key Components of PRA

The PRA service includes the following key components:

- Privileged Portals
- Privileged Consoles
- Privileged Approvals
- Privileged Credentials
- Privileged Policies
- Privileged Application Segments
- Diagnostics

## Supporting Features of PRA

Supporting PRA features includes:

- Emergency Access
- Arbitrary Authentication Domains
- File Transfer
- Clipboard
- Session Recording

## Understanding Key and Supporting PRA Components

To use PRA, you need to create a privileged portal with a privileged console that includes selected PRA-enabled applications. These are the main components of PRA. From there you can build upon the PRA features to provide a controlled experience, from authentication to using PRA, to reviewing and analyzing the usage of PRA.

Manage the PRA consoles after the PRA main components have been configured by including privileged approvals to set time limits on access. To provide ease of use, include a privileged credentials policy with selected privileged credentials.

Provide tools that the end user can use within a privileged console, include a privileged consoles policy to enable Clipboard, File Transfer, and Session Recording features. To enhance the security of uploaded files, configure the Internet & SaaS Sandbox File Transfer feature.

Gain deeper insight into PRA analytics by going to the User Activity Diagnostics page. Review and manage privileged session recordings by going to the Privileged Sessions page.

Privileged portals are what your end users use to gain access to designated servers and browsers for PRA. Privileged portals are designated with a URL and a Browser Access certificate that the Private Access (ZPA) infrastructure uses when an end user accesses a privileged portal. These can also be branded with the customer's domain and text.

An end user's privileged portal is commonly referred to as the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal. The PRA Portal is a user-friendly catalog of resources that shows what privileged consoles the end user can access after they have authenticated to the configured identity provider (IdP). The PRA Portal is external from the Zscaler Admin Console but its features are configured within the Zscaler Admin Console.

End users can also view future and expired privileged consoles, if any. If privileged approvals have been assigned to privileged consoles, then they expire following the scheduled window of time. If an end user has been given permissions for privileged live sessions, then there is also a carousel of the live privileged sessions they have access to. If you have included a notification banner, it appears at the top of the PRA Portal. After a privileged portal is created, privileged consoles can be added.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Portals](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-portals).

A privileged console is what the end user selects in a PRA Portal to access the assigned servers and databases associated with that privileged console. The privileged console and the PRA Portal are external to the Zscaler Admin Console, though they are configured within the Zscaler Admin Console. Privileged consoles are each assigned a protocol, domain, and port number. There are three types of protocols available to use with PRA: VNC, RealVNC, SSH, and RDP. End users can only access privileged consoles that they have been granted access to. End users can discover what privileged consoles they have access to by logging into the PRA Portal.

When an end user selects a privileged console, they are then required to provide their credentials specific to the associated protocol. After the end user is logged into the privileged console, there are a few features that are visible, if enabled for that privileged console. These options include a virtual keyboard, [File Transfer](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/uploading-and-downloading-file-transfer), and [Clipboard](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/copying-and-pasting-clipboard). If the [Session Recording feature](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-sessions) is enabled, then the end user sees a Recording notification at the top of the privileged console during their privileged session. If an end user has a [privileged approval](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-approvals) assigned to their privileged consoles, they lose access when the scheduled time expires.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Consoles](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-consoles).

A privileged approval is a set start and end date and time that an end user has access to a privileged console. After a time window expires, the end user can no longer access the privileged console. This is a key feature if you want to set permissions for contractors, third-party users, and other end users who only need a certain window of time for access.

Privileged consoles with privileged approvals that have ended due to the time window completing show as Expired. Any scheduled privileged consoles with upcoming time windows of access show as Future. Admins can clean up their privileged approvals table by purging expired privileged approvals.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Approvals](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-approvals).

Privileged credentials allow end users to seamlessly access privileged portals. These set credentials provide an end user access without requiring a personalized login for short-term end users (e.g., contractors and third-party users). To set a privileged credential with a privileged console, you need to [create a privileged credentials policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-privileged-credentials-policies).

To learn more, see [About Privileged Credentials](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-credentials).

There are two PRA-specific policies that can be set to provide rules for privileged consoles: privileged credentials policies and consoles policies. You might see both PRA policy options, only one, or neither in your Zscaler Admin Console depending on your enablement of these policy options.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-policy).

- Privileged Credential Policies
- Consoles Policies

Privileged credential policies allow you to assign existing [privileged credentials](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-credentials) to existing privileged consoles. When an end user accesses a privileged console that has an assigned privileged credentials policy, the end user can access the privileged console without manually logging in. If you delete the privileged credentials policy, the privileged credentials associated with the privileged consoles for that policy are removed and the privileged credential feature no longer applies to that privileged console. The credentials prompt the end user to log in, replacing the credential-provided access.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Credentials Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-credentials-policy).

Privileged consoles policies allow you to enable and disable the following features in a privileged console: [File Transfer](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/uploading-and-downloading-file-transfer), [Clipboard](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/copying-and-pasting-clipboard), and [Session Recording](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-sessions). You can enable or disable the items related to each of these features for each privileged consoles policy rule. Each item is disabled by default. The configurations you set in this policy rule determine what capabilities in a privileged console an end user has.

If enabled, the end user can access the File Transfer and Clipboard options from their designated icons in the privileged console window. If enabled, Session Recording shows as Recording at the top of the privileged console window. If any of the features are disabled, then they are not displayed, with the exception of the File Transfer feature, which shows if disabled but isn't functional.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Consoles Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-consoles-policy).

When you are [configuring a defined application segment](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-application-segments), you can enable PRA and assign a protocol to that application segment. When an application segment is PRA enabled, you can select that application segment when creating a privileged console. When an end user selects a privileged console in the PRA Portal, they are taken to the PRA-enabled application segment. When configuring a privileged console, you can only select application segments that aren't PRA enabled.

To learn more, see [About Privileged Remote Access Applications](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-remote-access-applications).

You can view the data and analytics for your PRA features on the User Activity Diagnostics page and the Privileged Sessions page. On the User Activity Diagnostics page, you can view data for Session Recordings, privileged credentials policies, privileged consoles policies, File Transfer, and PRA-related errors. In the User Activity Logs table, you can filter by policy and by Session Recording. The following fields are listed in the Policy column: Consoles Policy ID, File, and Credentials Policy ID. The following fields are listed in the Applications column: Credential Username, Credential Login Type, Files, PRA Error, and Session Recording. You can view the recorded privileged sessions when you click the Play icon in the Session Recording field.

To learn more, see [Accessing User Activity Diagnostics](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-user-activity-diagnostics).

You can view the data and analytics specific to privileged recorded sessions on the Privileged Sessions page on the Recorded tab. You can filter the data based on a protocol type. You can view and filter the data table that displays recorded privileged session details. If you want to play one of the recorded privileged sessions, click the Play button. This takes you to a new page to view the recording. You can also download a recording.

To learn more, see [Accessing Privileged Sessions](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-sessions).

Emergency access allows you to add end users access who only need access within a set window of time. You can designate one existing IdP to have emergency access for third-party users (e.g., contractors and vendors) provisioned to that IdP. When configuring a privileged approval, you can select the IdP with emergency access to apply the set date and time rules to the related emergency access users. The emergency access users are managed in an Okta IdP but can be viewed on the Emergency Access Users page within the Zscaler Admin Console.

To learn more, see [About Emergency Access Users](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-emergency-access-users).

Arbitrary authentication domains allow third-party end users to access a privileged portal with single sign-on for any authentication domain, without having to designate a specific domain. This streamlines the process of providing access to third-party users securely. You can enable arbitrary domains to one IdP at a time.

To learn more, see [Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-idp-single-sign).

File Transfer allows an end user to upload and download files within a privileged console if these features are enabled. You can enable these features when [configuring a privileged consoles policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-privileged-capabilities-policies). When an end user is in a privileged console, the File Transfer icon appears at the bottom of the page. If the upload feature is enabled, the end user can select files to upload from their local server to the privileged console. If the download feature is enabled, then the end user can select files within the privileged console to download to their local server.

To learn more, see [Uploading and Downloading with File Transfer](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/uploading-and-downloading-file-transfer).

In addition to uploading and downloading, if the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) Sandbox File Transfer feature is configured and enabled, then end users can inspect the files that they are uploading to prevent malicious files from being uploaded to the privileged console. This can be set up on the Integrations page and then enabled when [configuring a privileged consoles policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-privileged-capabilities-policies). When an end user is in a privileged console, the File Transfer icon appears at the bottom of the page. If the Inspect option is enabled, the end user can choose to inspect the selected files that are being uploaded from their local server to the privileged console. If the files inspected have malware detected, then the uploading process halts and the files are not uploaded.

To learn more, see [About Integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-integrations).

Clipboard allows an end user to copy and paste to and from the privileged console and their local system. You can enable the Clipboard Copy and Clipboard Paste features when you are [configuring a privileged consoles policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-privileged-capabilities-policies). If the copy or paste features are enabled, when an end user is in a privileged console, the Clipboard icon appears at the bottom of the page.

To learn more about this feature and its requirements, see [Copying and Pasting with Clipboard](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/copying-and-pasting-clipboard).

Privileged console sessions can be recorded and reviewed by admins. Viewing recorded privileged sessions allows admins to review malicious activity and error prevention. You can enable Record Sessions to have privileged sessions recorded for a privileged console when [configuring a privileged consoles policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-privileged-capabilities-policies). When an end user selects the privileged console with this policy configured, the Recording notification appears at the top of the screen within the privileged console window. After the end user ends the session for that privileged console, the recording for that privileged session ends. You can review the details of the privileged session and replay the recording by going to the Privileged Sessions page.

To learn more, see [Accessing Privileged Sessions](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-sessions).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/understanding-role-based-access-control-zpa-api","lastmod":"2026-06-01T12:01Z","nid":"1524436"} -->
## Understanding Role-Based Access Control for the ZPA API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-role-based-access-control-zpa-api
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > API Key Management > Understanding Role-Based Access Control for the ZPA API
- Last modified: 2026-06-01T12:01Z
- Summary: How to enforce RBAC for the publicly available ZPA API.

Role-based access control (RBAC) for all ZPA API operations ensures that access to API endpoints is restricted or granted based on user roles and permissions.

RBAC for ZPA API provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Enhance security and operational efficiency by ensuring that users only have access to the resources and actions necessary for their specific roles.
- Reduce the risk of unauthorized access and potential security breaches.

## Enforcing RBAC

To enforce RBAC for the ZPA API:

1. [Create a predefined or custom role](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-administrator-roles).
2. [Create an API client](https://help.zscaler.com/authentication-service/adding-api-client).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/understanding-server-client-connectivity","lastmod":"2026-04-02T16:17Z","nid":"1485581"} -->
## Understanding Server-to-Client Connectivity

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-server-client-connectivity
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Administration > Peer-to-Peer Connectivity > Understanding Server-to-Client Connectivity
- Last modified: 2026-04-02T16:17Z
- Summary: Information on server-to-client connectivity for use with remote assistance.

This feature is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.

In addition to connecting users to private applications, Private Access (ZPA) also supports connecting users to other Private Access-enabled devices for remote assistance.

Enabling server-to-client connectivity allows applications on your internal servers to connect through Branch Connectors and Cloud Connectors to endpoints running Zscaler Client Connector. This supports use cases such as remote troubleshooting and software distribution. Server-to-client connectivity allows you to connect to an end user's machine using a Zscaler IP address or FQDN from servers that don't have Zscaler Client Connector installed. This differs from the [client-to-client](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-client-client-connectivity) approach where the connectivity is between two endpoints running Zscaler Client Connector. A Zscaler IP, which is a virtual IP address maintained by Zscaler, makes any end user's machine reachable via the Cloud or Branch Connectors for server-to-client connectivity. To learn more, see [About Client Connector IP Assignment](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-client-connector-ip-assignment).

The following diagram shows the network flow for server-to-client connectivity.

[Image: ​​​​Server-to-client connectivity flow chart diagram]

If you are leveraging virtual Zscaler IP-based connectivity:

- A client or endpoint enrolls in peer-to-peer connectivity when [validating a client hostname](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/validating-client-hostname).
- Zscaler assigns a virtual Zscaler IP address from the configured IP range (e.g., 192.168.254.0/24). You can then download the IP assignment details as a CSV file. To learn more, see [About IP Bindings](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-ip-bindings).
- The cloud applications or on-premises applications initiate connectivity to the client over the virtual Zscaler IP address (192.168.254.0/24) on a specific port (e.g., 445).
- Cloud or Branch Connector (as applicable and based on your policy criteria) intercepts these outgoing requests from the applications and forwards them to the Zscaler cloud for connectivity to the client or endpoint.

You can also achieve the virtual IP-based connectivity workflows using FQDN connectivity, depending on how your tools connect with the endpoints.

To successfully enable server-to-client connectivity, the end user must:

- Have [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/understanding-zscaler-client-connector-app-downloads) on their device with Private Access enabled.
- Deploy a Cloud or Branch Connector. To learn more, see [Zscaler Cloud and Branch Connector Help](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/getting-started).
- If you are deploying Cloud or Branch Connector specifically for server-to-client connectivity through an FQDN, Zscaler recommends you configure conditional DNS forwarding so only the DNS requests from the applications requiring server-to-client connections are forwarded to the Cloud or Branch Connector.
- Update routing to ensure the Zscaler IP ranges traverse the Cloud or Branch Connector (e.g., 100.64.0.0/16 gateway = BranchConnectorGroup1).
- Define Zscaler virtual IP ranges or subnets along with the location attribute in Private Access that is assigned to Zscaler Client Connectors. The IP address or subnet is then assigned to Zscaler Client Connector from the defined IP ranges.
- Configure application segments and access policies in Private Access either with FQDNs of endpoints or virtual IP ranges or subnets that are assigned to Zscaler Client Connector.

The admin then uses their third-party tool (i.e., Microsoft Configuration Manager) to launch remote assistance to workstations by using the FQDNs or virtual Zscaler IP addresses. The Cloud or Branch Connector then forwards these requests to the Private Access cloud to begin connections with Zscaler Client Connector. Zscaler Client Connector then completes the connection and sends the request back to the server. To learn more, see [Configuring Server-To-Client Connectivity](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-server-client-connectivity).

The following functions and features are not supported for server-to-client connectivity based on the virtual Zscaler IP:

- [Configuring a forwarding profile action for ZIA](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/configuring-forwarding-profiles-zscaler-client-connector#forwarding-profile-action-zia) using DTLA
- [Disaster Recovery](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-disaster-recovery)
- [Machine Tunnels](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/deploying-machine-tunnels-pre-windows-login)
- [Microtenants](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-microtenants)
- [Zscaler Client Connector Support for Multiple Tenants](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-client-connector-support-multiple-tenants). This limitation applies if those tenants correspond to partner tenants, or when a user is logged in to a partner tenant.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
